title: Photographic plates show a faint state of at least 19 years (1974-1993) of the extreme-dust dimmer G2874 and a dip of at least 2 mag of the dimmer G2698 in 1987
abstract: Deep, aperiodic dust dimming of main-sequence field dwarfs is known only from data after 2004. We asked if the dimmers also dimmed decades ago. We used DASCH Harvard plates (1889-1989) and our own photometry of Digitized Sky Survey plates (POSS-I, Quick-V, POSS-II, SERC; 1950-1998) for 10 campaign dimmers, with matched control stars on the same plates, Gaia XP or Pan-STARRS1 calibration, and ZTF quiet levels. The extreme-dust dimmer G2874 (Gaia DR3 2874265305022213760, G = 12.8) was at its Gaia XP B level in 1920-1953 (-0.11 and +0.01 mag; 168 plates) but +0.41 and +0.36 mag fainter in 1965-1978 and 1978-1989 (68 plates). Its change, +0.42 mag, is a 7.3-sigma outlier among 131 field stars (-0.002 +- 0.058 mag; none above 0.2). Independent DSS plates agree: normal in 1952; +0.29 +- 0.07 (V, 1982), +0.14 +- 0.07 (R, 1991) and +0.69 +- 0.13 (B, 1993); +0.04 +- 0.13 (I, 1995). The faint state was red (A proportional to lambda^-2.1, 95 percent 0.9-5.9; grey disfavoured), like the modern ZTF dips (2.5-2.8). It started between 1953 and 1974 and ended between 1994 and 2014; Gaia XP and ZTF show the bright level now. Thus the occulter covered the star for at least 19 years, about 13 orbits at the 230 K dust radius: a long-lived extended dust structure, not a single clump. The M0 dimmer G2698 (Gaia DR3 2698173741829957888) is not detected on the POSS-II J plate of 1987 August (S/N -0.2), which detects 88-97 percent of field stars up to 2 mag fainter than its quiet level; it is detected on the 1953 plates and on the 1995 plates (1995 July: +0.72 +- 0.17 mag in r). Thus it had a dip of at least 2 mag 23 years before its earliest known dips. For Gaia20cdd, G2870, G2796, G3768, Gaia20bkx and G4466, 4-5 plate epochs show no significant fade, but this outcome has a probability of 0.65-0.95 under their ZTF activity, so the plates do not constrain them. Limitations: after 1965 the G2874 Harvard data come from one plate series; the onset falls in a plate gap; the G2698 result rests on one plate; faint-star plate photometry has about 0.1 mag systematic error; no spectra.
